question: Who wrote the novel ‘Vanity Fair’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**William Thackeray**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **William Makepeace Thackeray** is the author of the novel **'Vanity Fair'**, which was first published in 1848.
 
• The novel is a satirical representation of British society during the early 19th century, often described as a "novel without a hero."
 
• 'Vanity Fair' primarily revolves around two main characters, Becky Sharp and Amelia Sedley, exploring themes such as ambition, morality, and social climbing.
 
• The title 'Vanity Fair' refers to an allegorical location from John Bunyan's 'Pilgrim's Progress,' symbolizing human frailty and worldly temptations.
 
• Thackeray's work is regarded as a masterpiece of English literature, showcasing his sharp wit, narrative innovation, and social critique.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **William Makepeace Thackeray**

 
 
• Thackeray (1811–1863) was a renowned English novelist and satirist, best known for his critical portrayal of English upper-class society.
 
• His other notable works include 'The History of Pendennis' and 'The Luck of Barry Lyndon.'
 
• Thackeray's literary style often involved humor, irony, and vivid character development.
 
• He was a contemporary of Charles Dickens, although their writing styles differed significantly.
 
 
 
• **Victorian Literature**
 
 
• The Victorian era (1837–1901) witnessed significant literary achievements, with authors like Charles Dickens, George Eliot, and Thackeray shaping English literature.
 
• Key themes included social reform, industrialization, class dynamics, and moral dilemmas.
 
 
 
• **Satire in Literature**
 
 
• Satire is a literary genre that uses humor, irony, and ridicule to criticize societal norms and human behavior.
 
• Thackeray's 'Vanity Fair' is considered a prime example of satire in English literature.
